to: CrazyGames game review team via the Developer Portal
subject: HTML5 review: Tower Drop — Stack blocks with precision — keep the tower balanced
body:
Hello CrazyGames review team,

I am submitting Tower Drop for an initial editorial/technical fit review. It is a self-contained HTML5 game: Stack blocks with precision — keep the tower balanced. The live build is https://hfo-games.pages.dev/games/021_tower_drop/.

Why it may fit CrazyGames: short-session HTML5 fit, existing cover/screenshot, and readiness to follow the current SDK review path. The package is a short-session, dependency-free browser build with a prepared cover image and screenshot. No portal submission, SDK call, ad integration, or external post was performed by the staging run.

This is not an isolated prototype. The full, no-login portfolio at https://hfo-games.pages.dev/ contains 21 live HTML5 titles. Four distinct Suika DLC deployments are also available for comparison: https://hfo-suika-dlc-1-norse.pages.dev/, https://hfo-suika-dlc-2-crystal.pages.dev/, https://hfo-suika-dlc-3-yinyang.pages.dev/, https://hfo-suika-dlc-4-alchemy.pages.dev/. I am highlighting Tower Drop because its action loop is more legible than sending an indiscriminate catalogue dump.

Would you review this build and identify the first blocking item for portal acceptance? If the answer is no, a short reason—gameplay fit, polish, performance, SDK, or catalogue overlap—would be useful feedback.

— TTaoGaming
https://github.com/TTaoGaming
canon_priority_note: Poki is low-priority per Sigrun V3; staged because the operator explicitly included Poki as a source. Approve selectively.
